ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Act 2023; Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Public Act 2013 No 69); Terrorism Suppression Act 2002 (Public Act 2002 No 34); Companies (Ultimate Holding Company Information) Regulations 2018; and Companies (Fees) Regulations 2010, together with the Sanctions Act 2021 designations administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. New Zealand does not maintain a public UBO registry; beneficial ownership is obtained by reporting entities under AML/CFT obligations and held confidentially, accessible to supervisors and law enforcement.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in an Apostille Convention country: obtain a certified copy from the Companies Office and then apply for a Hague Apostille through the Department of Internal Affairs (Authentications Unit), New Zealand. For use in a non-member state: apply for full consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the New Zealand embassy or consulate in the destination state. These two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: request a certified Certificate of Good Standing and then apply for a Hague Apostille from the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs (Authentications Unit) if the destination is an Apostille state. Consular path: notarize the certificate, have it authenticated by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and then legalize it at the destination country's consular post. Do not use both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing local director, registered agent, and bank account signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the parent/shareholder company, or the sole shareholder as applicable, executed before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the signatory is in an Apostille Convention state: notarize the resolution or power of attorney before a local notary, then obtain an Apostille from that country's designated Competent Authority. If the signatory is in a non-member state: notarize, obtain country-of-origin foreign ministry authentication, and then obtain consular legalization from the New Zealand embassy or consulate having consular authority. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes; they cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitution of the New Zealand limited company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (constitutional documents as filed); certified true copy may be issued by the company secretary or the Registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: request a certified copy from the Companies Office and apostillize it with the Department of Internal Affairs (New Zealand) for use in an Apostille state. Consular route: have the certified copy notarized, processed by MFAT legalization, and then presented to the consulate of the destination state. Use only one route according to the destination country's Hague Apostille membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (shareholder/parent company creditworthiness and good conduct)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Paying bank of the ultimate beneficial owner or corporate shareholder, with banker's signature notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: the banker's signature is notarized and the notary's certificate receives an Apostille from the relevant Competent Authority. For non-Apostille states: the notarized bank letter must pass through the country's foreign ministry or equivalent competent authority and then be legalized by the New Zealand consulate or diplomatic mission in that country. Never combine the apostille and consular legalization procedures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 12-21 (incorporation and registration), ss 122-127 (registered office), ss 128-131 (share rights), ss 151-153 (appointment and consent of directors), and s 41 (consideration for shares)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Registration Service, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand; digital lodgement through the New Zealand Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Act 1993, s 12), lodged electronically with the New Zealand Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 does not impose a minimum issued capital or paid-up capital on a limited liability company. Shares may be allotted with no par value and for consideration set by the directors. No blocked escrow account requirement exists for the specified Design-as-a-Service subscription business.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF NZ_LTD

This First Board Resolution is made on the date of incorporation and recorded in the minutes of the inaugural meeting of the Board of Directors of NZ_LTD, a company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand.

RESOLVED that:

1. Share Capital and Subscription. The Board acknowledges that the founding shareholder has offered to subscribe for the full initial issued ordinary shares of the Company at no par value, and that no minimum paid-up share capital is required under New Zealand law. The Board resolves to accept the subscription and to allot such shares in accordance with the share subscription record, to enter the subscription amount and allotment date in the share register, and to issue the corresponding share certificates or electronic records if requested.

2. Issue of Shares as Service Consideration. The Board confirms that any issued shares may lawfully be paid in cash or non-cash consideration under s 41 of the Companies Act 1993, and for avoidance of doubt the Design-as-a-Service digital subscription business does not require any mandated escrow deposit or capital blockage.

3. Banking. The Board authorizes the directors to open and maintain such bank and payment accounts as are required, including accounts with a New Zealand registered bank and the payment rails Stripe_Billing and Wise. The Board approves the adoption of a bank mandate under which any two directors or other named signatories may sign cheques and electronic instructions. The secretary is directed to deliver a certified copy of this resolution to any bank or payment institution.

4. Registered Office. The Board adopts the registered office of the Company as stated in the application for registration, declares that address to be the Company's address for service, and instructs the directors and secretary to notify the Registrar of any future change in address using the prescribed form.

5. Statutory Officers. The Board appoints the named individuals as directors of the Company, and appoints a secretary or other officer if required by the Company's constitution. Each such officer has consented to act and shall hold office in accordance with ss 151 to 153 of the Companies Act 1993.

6. Tax and Authority. The Board authorizes the directors and secretary to apply to Inland Revenue for the Company's IRD number, GST registration, and any required Pay As You Earn obligations, and to execute all statutory filings with the Companies Office.

7. Effectiveness. This Resolution is effective immediately and may be relied upon by third parties as full authority for the actions described.

This Resolution is signed by the Chairperson and recorded in the Company's board minute book.

Dated this ___ day of ______ 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office through the New Zealand Companies Register online search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the full proposed company name in the New Zealand Companies Register. If another entity has an identical or confusingly similar name, select a distinctive alternative or obtain the written consent of the existing proprietor and file that consent. Submit the name-search request to the Registrar through the online incorporation portal. The applicant must verify that the name does not violate the Companies Act 1993, does not imply Crown approval, and does not contain a restricted word requiring consent from a relevant Ministry or professional body. Retain the search result reference number for inclusion in the formation application.
required_dossiers: Identity and address details of the applicant
Written consent from existing proprietor if a similar name is submitted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on similarity grounds, choose an alternative distinctive name and resubmit; if the refusal is based on a restricted expression, furnish written consent from the relevant Ministry or professional body and apply for Registrar direction under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the New Zealand Companies Register using the authorized agent or director profile and proceed to the Register a Company module. Enter the company name, registered office address, directors, shareholders, share structure and any constitution text. Each director and shareholder must consent electronically, and for overseas applicants certified identity documents must be uploaded. Elect to adopt the Companies Act default constitution or file a custom constitution. Attach the registered office consent and address for service. Review the draft application for accuracy, pay the applicable filing fee by card, and submit. After registration the system issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a Companies number. Retain the certificate and the electronic registry extract as legal proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Director consent forms and identity verification documents
Registered office address consent from the office holder
Address for service for the company in New Zealand
AML/CFT verification records for any non-resident applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is placed on query, address the Registrar's information request within 20 working days, re-upload corrected consents, and request prioritisation on the Companies Office service desk. If the application is declined, file a fresh application after curing the defect and seek a formal review if the decision appears legally erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax Registration and Business Number Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand, through the business registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Incorporation and Companies number to register the company with Inland Revenue through the online business registration portal. Confirm the company's primary business activity as ISIC 7410 specialised design activities. Determine GST status by reference to expected taxable turnover; registration is compulsory if turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period and may be voluntary earlier. If employees are engaged, register for PAYE, ESCT and KiwiSaver. Obtain the IRD number and complete the online business profile. File a GST return and make tax payments through IRD secure online services when due. Keep the IRD number and registration confirmations in the corporate file.
required_dossiers: New Zealand registered office and service address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a compliance query, respond with the Certificate of Incorporation and a complete explanation of the business model, correct the industry classification code, and use IRD secure online services to remedy any under-registration before penalty notices become final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand registered bank and licensed payment service providers for Stripe_Billing and Wise
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the board resolution authorising bank accounts and payment rails, then present a certified copy to a New Zealand registered bank or licensed payment provider for due diligence. Complete customer due diligence forms for the legal entity, directors and any 25% beneficial owner, and provide proof of registered office address. Use the payment rails Stripe_Billing and Wise for subscription collection and settlement; Stripe requires the company website, business model narrative and processing forecasts. Wait for account activations and execute separate banking mandates in accordance with the resolution. Submit the signed bank mandate, certificate of incorporation, IRD confirmation and beneficial ownership declaration.
required_dossiers: First Board resolution adopting bank signatories
Director photographic identification and proof of address
Registered office address proof and service address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment provider rejects the application, supplement the beneficial ownership evidence or company operational details, obtain a current Companies Office extract, and escalate within the provider's relationship management team; transfer to another New Zealand registered bank if non-resolution persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Register Maintenance and Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register, with internal company secretary administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the statutory registers and company records at the registered office, including the share register, director register, minute book and accounting records required under the Companies Act 1993. File the annual return with the Companies Office before the return date, confirming current directors, address for service and shareholders. Report any changes of director or registered office online within 20 working days. The company secretary or authorised administrator should run periodic register extracts from the Companies Register to verify data consistency and lodge any corrections. Where a director or beneficial owner changes, update the underlying register and file the required notices; preserving governance continuity is critical for the design subscription agency.
required_dossiers: Notification forms for director or registered office changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is late or a register is found defective, file the overdue return, pay the late filing penalty if the statute prescribes it, file a rectification application with supporting board resolution and evidence, and notify the Registrar in writing of any data mismatch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. New Zealand imposes no industrial licensing board obligation for ISIC 7410 specialized design activities because the entity conducts pure digital product interface design and subscription services without physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No operational or manufacturing permit is required for a Design-as-a-Service digital subscription agency under ISIC 7410.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. No New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority or regional council resource consent is required for a pure digital design subscription business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. ISIC 7410 is not a permitted activity requiring a full EIA, environmental registration, or resource consent classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The business generates no wastewater, VOC emissions, hazardous waste, or industrial discharges, so no quantitative environmental discharge thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. The company does not operate a physical factory, plant, warehouse, or hazardous goods site, so no Civil Defence fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or site-based workplace safety approval is required. General obligations under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 remain applicable only to any ordinary office or home-workplace administration of the digital design agency.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake); online taxpayer portal: myIR secure online services; company incorporation registry: New Zealand Companies Office / Companies Register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand-incorporated limited company, the IRD number is obtained through the Companies Office registration workflow or by post-registration application via myIR. Required particulars include certificate of incorporation, New Zealand registered office address, directors and shareholders, constitution or articles of association, and intended tax registration dates. For a foreign non-resident company not incorporated in New Zealand, the entity must apply to Inland Revenue using form IR596 (Non-resident company IRD number application), providing foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution, appointment of a New Zealand tax agent or resident contact for service of notices, proof of business address or fixed establishment in New Zealand, and financial projections demonstrating actual or intended taxable activity. Inland Revenue issues the same IRD number for income tax, GST, and employer obligations. A non-resident entity that has New Zealand taxable activity or that supplies remote services to New Zealand consumers above the GST threshold may apply for GST registration simultaneously.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not have a general check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include the Look-Through Company election under the Income Tax Act 2007 (subpart HB), the consolidated group company election for wholly-owned corporate groups under section FM 31 of the Income Tax Act 2007, and GST group treatment under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid and branch mismatch rules under sections FH 1 to FH 11 of the Income Tax Act 2007 apply mandatorily; there is no elective opt-out for hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (section 51); non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers have the same NZD 60,000 threshold under the remote services GST regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance regime, government invoice API pre-approval, or anti-fraud digital stamping. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and supported through the Peppol interoperability framework. GST tax invoices must contain the statutory particulars required by section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and may be issued in paper or electronic form. Buyer-created tax invoices are permitted under section 24G. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR; transactional invoice clearance is not required, but zero-rated export invoices should state the zero-rating basis and be supported by the export documentation bundle.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when they are exported from New Zealand by the supplier within 28 days of the time of supply. Services are zero-rated under section 11A when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not in New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are not directly connected with New Zealand land or goods. For remote services such as UI/UX design subscriptions supplied on a B2B basis to an overseas non-resident business customer, zero-rating is available when the recipient is not in New Zealand and the place-of-supply rules in section 8B do not treat the supply as made to a New Zealand consumer. The same service supplied to a New Zealand-resident consumer is standard-rated GST at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs export entry filed through the New Zealand Trade Single Window or CusMod, identifying the exporter, destination, goods description, HS classification, and export date.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing that the goods physically departed New Zealand.
Commercial invoice and sales contract matching the GST tax invoice and confirming the overseas buyer.
NZ Customs cargo movement or outward export report showing exit from New Zealand.

Bank settlement evidence, including SWIFT MT103, New Zealand bank foreign-currency credit advice, or overseas payment receipt; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a statutory instrument under New Zealand law.

For services-only exports: signed SaaS subscription agreement, one-time or recurring payment evidence, user records showing non-resident customer location, and IP deliverable acceptance records to substantiate the offshore recipient.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may assess GST on an export supply at the standard 15% rate, together with use-of-money interest, if the zero-rating is not substantiated by contemporaneous customs, transport, contract, and payment evidence. Records supporting zero-rated exports must be retained for seven years under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 include 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 50% where an unacceptable tax position has a dominant purpose of tax avoidance, and up to 150% for evasion or similar conduct. Fraudulent export documentation or intent to defeat GST may also expose directors and shareholders to criminal liability under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and penalties under the Crimes Act 1961. Inland Revenue can amend assessments within four years for non-specified matters, with no time limit in cases of evasion; clawback will include reversal of input credits previously attributable to the export supply and any refund obtained.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fundamentally liberalised foreign exchange regime characterized by full current account and capital account convertibility of the New Zealand dollar. There are no exchange control approvals, quantitative limits, or surrender-to-custodian requirements on the receipt, retention, or repatriation of foreign currency. Both capital inflows and outflows, including equity injections, intercompany loans, dividend repatriation, profit remittances, loan repayments, and trade-related settlements, may be freely routed through any registered commercial bank. Non-resident shareholders may own a New Zealand limited company without exchange-control attraction, provided the underlying business does not involve sensitive land or significant business assets that trigger the Overseas Investment Act 2005. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is the central bank and prudential regulator, supervising banks and payment systems rather than operating a foreign exchange approval desk. The practical constraints on convertibility today are therefore not statutory exchange controls but bank-level AML/CFT onboarding, sanctions screening, source-of-funds verification, and the obligation on the company to meet New Zealand resident withholding tax and non-resident withholding tax rules when distributing funds. Profit remittance to shareholders is lawful and unrestricted once the entity has satisfied Companies Office filings, tax payments, and the bank's economic substance questioning about beneficial ownership. No special central bank permission is required for payment routing, forward hedging, foreign currency accounts, or multicurrency balances, making the New Zealand jurisdiction highly suitable for an international design-as-a-service treasury structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules in New Zealand. An exporter or design-subscription supplier may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in any onshore or connected foreign currency account, may settle immediately into NZD at a free market price, or may hold the funds offshore without conversion; there is no mandatory conversion ratio and no surrender timeline imposed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and fintech payment platforms receive a Low-to-Medium rating as the sole treasury bank relationship but a High rating as ancillary cross-border settlement rails for a low-risk design subscription business. The Banking Prudential Supervision regime in New Zealand restricts deposit-taking from the public to registered banks; an offshore EMI or e-money institution is not a compliant substitute for a domestic bank operating account, capital escrow relationship, trade finance facility, or foreign exchange hedging line. Wise is viable for receiving design-client subscription collections and for low-value disbursements to overseas designers because it is registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register and provides transparent multi-currency FX. Stripe is viable as a recurring payment gateway for UI/UX subscription invoices, but funds settled through Stripe and Wise must be swept into the prime New Zealand Tier 1 bank account to maintain a clear audit trail for capital verification, tax filings, and bank covenant purposes. An offshore EMI that is not registered as a financial service provider in New Zealand and does not maintain an NZD clearing relationship with a registered bank should be rejected for any balance above daily operating contingency thresholds. The primary liquidity hub should always be a locally incorporated commercial bank that can issue SWIFT instructions, accept inbound investor money, perform OFAC/sanctions screening, and support documentary trade instruments without regulatory ambiguity.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT regulation does not require every statutory director to appear physically in a bank branch for a straightforward low-risk corporate onboarding. Banks routinely accept remote identity verification through independent digital verification platforms, certified true copies, and a recorded video interview for directors and beneficial owners. However, most Tier 1 banks retain a branch-level discretion to require the founding director or a New Zealand-resident authorising officer to attend an in-person appointment when the entity has offshore shareholders, trust structures, or unusual source-of-wealth documentation. Remote consular proxy opening is not a generally accepted practice; instead, the first director can complete a ledger-verified video call, the beneficial owner can provide certified passports and utility invoices, and the company secretary can sign the bank mandate in New Zealand under power of attorney. For this NZ limited company, an efficient onboarding plan is to appoint a New Zealand-resident company administration officer as the on-the-ground relationship contact while the ultimate beneficial owners participate in remote interviews and upload notarised corporate records. Banks will typically request the board resolution, Certificate of Incorporation, company constitution, register of directors and shareholders, and proof of the active UI/UX subscription service before allowing the account to transact.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a New Zealand Company (Companies Act 1993, section 210)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the company's annual registration anniversary date (the 'Return Date'); the filing window opens 1 month before and closes 1 month after the Return Date, and the Return must be lodged by the Return Date to avoid late fees.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing automatically incurs a NZ$50 late fee (approx. USD 31) in addition to the base fee; failure to file after the Return Date triggers a default notice from the Registrar, and continued absence of filing for two consecutive year dates may result in administrative strike-off from the Companies Register under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993, leading to dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report (if mandatory) filed with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the company's balance date for entities required to file under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, or within 20 working days after the later of the shareholders' meeting approval and the signing date of the financial statements, whichever applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file required financial statements or audit report is an offence under section 44 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013, carrying a maximum fine of NZ$50,000 per officer; non-compliance can also lead to enforcement action, director disqualification, and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit is legally mandated where the company (or its consolidated group) is classified as 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, which occurs when for each of the two most recent accounting periods the entity meets any one of: (a) total assets exceed NZ$60 million (approx. USD 37.2 million); (b) total revenue exceeds NZ$30 million (approx. USD 18.6 million); or (c) it has 100 or more full-time equivalent employees. Audit is also mandatory for publicly accountable entities, for overseas-owned companies (beneficial ownership >25% outside New Zealand), for any company whose constitution requires an audit, and in cases where shareholders holding 5% or more of the voting rights give written notice requiring an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB); large entities must apply New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS), while non-large entities without public accountability may apply NZ IFRS for SMEs (or the Reduced Disclosure Regime where eligible).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a separate UBO registry. The annual return to the Companies Office constitutes the annual statutory confirmation of all registered shareholders, share classes, and directors. Any share transfer must be recorded in the company's own register of members within 30 days of the transfer notice, and any share allotment or change of director must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the company or its reporting agent must identify and verify beneficial owners at engagement and maintain updated beneficial ownership information for AML/CFT purposes, with changes in qualifying ownership (typically above 25%) being captured and risk-assessed on an ongoing basis.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand has no patent box. The main preferential regime is the Research and Development Tax Incentive (RDTI) granting a refundable 15% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure. Other effective rate reductions arise from imputation credits, the domestic loss ring-fencing rules, and the absence of a distributed profits tax at entity level. For design-as-a-service subscription businesses, only genuine R&D activity that meets the statutory definition in Income Tax Act 2007 s LA 5 is eligible.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory year cap) but carried-forward losses are forfeited unless a 49% shareholder continuity test is maintained; alternatively, the business continuity test may preserve losses if the same or similar business is carried on.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Tax Return (with supporting IR10 financial statements where required) filed electronically through Inland Revenue myIR portal. Non-resident companies deriving New Zealand-source income must also comply with NRWT obligations on the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the end of the tax year. For non-standard balance dates, the filing deadline is the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date. Provisional tax instalments are generally due in three instalments during the year, and terminal tax is due on the same 7th day of the fourth month after balance date unless a tax agent extension applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income derived from the company’s business, including UI/UX design subscription fees, consulting charges, licence fees for design assets, and all other assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company filing IR4 must declare New Zealand-source income under ITA 2007 source rules, including services physically performed in New Zealand, subscriptions derived from New Zealand users, and intellectual property used in New Zealand. Cross-border subscription income must be apportioned on a per-user or per-subscriber basis; a foreign parent or affiliate receiving residual global fees may trigger a transfer pricing adjustment. Any income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment must be fully disclosed, and no deduction may be claimed for distributions to shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure, including staff salaries, subcontractor costs, software hosting, marketing, office rent, legal/compliance fees, and amortisation of capitalised design assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must satisfy the general permission and capital limitation in ITA 2007 ss DA 1-DA 2. For cross-border related-party transactions, only arm’s-length expenses are deductible. Payments to offshore related design contractors, foreign marketing agents, or group service companies must be supported by benchmarking studies and New Zealand transfer pricing documentation. Interest deductions are limited under the interest limitation rules for residential property but generally available for a genuine design agency; nevertheless, thin capitalisation rules apply to non-resident-controlled companies, capping debt deductions where New Zealand shareholder debt exceeds 110% of worldwide debt in the 75%+ foreign-controlled group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or tax loss after applying all available deductions, including depreciation and amortisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the return shows a loss, the non-resident company must prove continuity of shareholder ownership or business continuity before carrying the loss forward. A change in the beneficial ownership of the NZ Ltd to a newly established offshore trust or foreign holding company may permanently destroy carried-forward tax losses. The IR4 should reflect only genuine commercial losses after eliminating transfer pricing undercharges to offshore related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward and imputation credit account position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company must disclose the imputation credit account (ICA) balance and attach dividend imputation schedules if any distributions were made. Non-resident shareholders should be informed that dividends with imputation credits may be subject to lower NRWT only if fully imputed and the shareholder is entitled to treaty benefits. The ICA must not go into debit; a debit balance triggers supplementary dividend rules and resident withholding tax obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation at the corporate rate of 28%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the flat 28% rate to net taxable income. Non-resident companies are not entitled to the Australia/NZ or Korean tax credit rules unless a treaty applies. The New Zealand branch profits of a non-resident company are subject to the same 28% rate; there is no separate branch profits tax, but branch remittances may be treated as dividends for NRWT when the company is an offshore insurer or bank in particular circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, including PAYE withholdings, provisional tax payments, resident withholding tax (RWT), foreign tax credits, imputation credits, and RDTI credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company can claim foreign tax credits for foreign-source income included in the New Zealand return, subject to the limitation in ITA 2007 s LJ 6. If the foreign income has already borne tax in a treaty jurisdiction, the credit is limited to the New Zealand tax payable on that income. The RDTI tax credit is claimed using the supplementary R&D form and reduces tax payable or produces a refund for loss-making companies, but the credit attaches to eligible expenditure actually incurred in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable or refund due after applying credits, provisional tax, and use-of-money interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any terminal tax must be paid by the statutory due date. If the company is non-resident and has only New Zealand-source income subject to final NRWT, it may not need to file an IR4 at all, but if it has a New Zealand taxable presence or has chosen to return rental/schedular income, it must file. Where the company fails to withhold NRWT from outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, Inland Revenue can assess the company jointly and severally with the recipient for the unpaid NRWT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary schedule: related-party disclosures and transfer pricing information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IR4 return portal asks whether the company has entered into cross-border related-party transactions. If annual related-party transactions exceed the New Zealand documentation threshold, the company must prepare a Local File and, where applicable, a Master File. A non-resident-controlled NZ design subscription agency charging low-margin design services to an offshore parent is a typical audit target; the return must disclose the transfer pricing method selected and the arm’s-length outcome.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 attracts a $250 late filing penalty, plus a further $250 for each month of continued non-filing. Late payment of tax triggers an initial late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax plus a further 1% per month while the shortfall remains outstanding. Use-of-money interest accrues on unpaid and overpaid tax at rates set by Inland Revenue. Deliberate exclusion of income or overstatement of deductions is an abusive tax position subject to a 100% shortfall penalty, increasing to 150% for evasion. Criminal tax evasion carries prosecution under the Crimes Act 1961 and Tax Administration Act 1994, with imprisonment up to 3 years for evasion of assessment and up to 7 years for evasion of payment, plus director disqualification and departure prohibition orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory NRWT on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident is 15% where the dividend is fully imputed with New Zealand imputation credits, and 30% where the dividend is not fully imputed. Dividends paid within a wholly-owned group may be exempt from NRWT under the supplementary dividend rules only if specific administrative conditions are met. Under most NZ DTA protocols, the treaty dividend rate is 15% for portfolio shareholders and can be reduced to 5% for a corporate shareholder holding at least 10-15% of the voting power, subject to the limitation-on-benefits or principal purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority evidencing residence, submit a valid beneficial ownership declaration, and provide the NZ payer with a completed IR291 Application for reduced non-resident withholding rate. The payer must retain this documentation before filing the NRWT return; the beneficiary must be the beneficial owner of the dividend, not an intermediary, nominee, or conduit. The NZ resident company must also ensure the shareholder is not treaty shopping: Inland Revenue will apply the principal purpose test under the MLI and the relevant DTA. Where a TRC is unavailable, the statutory 15% or 30% NRWT rate must be withheld. If the DTA claim is rejected, the payee may apply to Inland Revenue for a refund of the excess NRWT under Tax Administration Act 1994; however, the refund is not available where the recipient has not satisfied the beneficial ownership test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory NRWT rate for cross-border royalties and interest is 15%. An Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply instead of NRWT to interest paid by an approved issuer on registered securities, provided the lender is not a related party of the issuer. Treaty rates generally reduce royalty and interest withholding to 10% or 0% depending on the DTA partner. For royalties, the copyright, design, trade-mark, or know-how payment must not exceed an arm’s-length rate; the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines must be applied when the royalty is paid to an offshore related company. For interest, a non-resident parent lending to its NZ subsidiary must respect the arm’s-length interest rate and the thin capitalisation safe harbour; excessive interest is recharacterised as a dividend or denied deduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 for annual cross-border related-party transactions (each transaction category or aggregate related-party dealings above this level requires a Local File). A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue above NZD 680,000,000, following the OECD BEPS Action 13 template. New Zealand transfer pricing rules also require contemporaneous documentation, typically prepared within 30 days of the return filing date or before the tax position is taken.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate the Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance is a decisive legal factor in three areas: (1) tax residence – a company incorporated in NZ is resident unless its centre of management is elsewhere, and an offshore-managed NZ company may be non-resident if a tie-breaker treaty clause applies; (2) permanent establishment – a foreign parent of the NZ design agency must not create a taxable PE in NZ through employees or dependent agents; (3) DTA entitlement – the NZ entity must be the beneficial owner of the design IP and must perform core income-generating activities (CIGA) in New Zealand, including strategic design decisions, client contracting, risk assumption, and senior management of subscription operations. A shell NZ Ltd that merely holds the design subscription contract while all substantive activities occur offshore will be ignored for tax purposes, and the profits will be reallocated under the OECD BEPS rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Sham Substance and Artificial Profit Extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ Ltd invoices the full UI/UX subscription fee to foreign clients, then pays a 90% service fee to an offshore affiliate in a no-tax jurisdiction for alleged ‘group design consultancy’ that in fact performs no services. The NZ company has no employees, no office, and does not exercise real decision-making; the arrangement has no commercial purpose other than eroding the NZ tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 s BG 1 and s GB 1 permit Inland Revenue to reconstruct the transaction and disregard the artificial company. Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141A-141EB impose a shortfall penalty of 100% for an abusive tax position and 150% for evasion, plus use-of-money interest. Under the Crimes Act 1961 s 144A, a person who evades assessment of tax is liable to imprisonment for up to 3 years; under s 144B, evasion of payment of tax carries imprisonment for up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the company is a facade for tax evasion. Directors who signed the sham service agreements or directed profit shifting are jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax shortfall to the extent they received a benefit or actively participated. Inland Revenue can issue a departure prohibition order, freezing exit from New Zealand, and can institute civil asset recovery under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009. Directors may also be disqualified from managing companies under the Companies Act 1993 for up to 10 years and face criminal imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Failure to Produce Contemporaneous Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ design subscription company pays an excessively high royalty or intercompany service charge to its non-resident parent for the use of the parent’s ‘brand and design algorithms’, without performing a comparability analysis, without any royalty calculation, and without preparing a Local File despite related-party transactions exceeding the NZD 1,000,000 threshold. The pricing is not at arm’s length and shifts New Zealand profit to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 6 to s GC 18 require the Commissioner to adjust the taxable income to an arm’s-length amount. Failure to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation exposes the company to a 20% shortfall penalty for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for an abusive tax position. The Tax Administration Act 1994 also imposes a separate penalty for failing to disclose cross-border transactions, and the group may be required to file a Country-by-Country Report; non-filing attracts $1,000 penalty for each failure and further penalties for each month of non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve a non-arm’s-length intercompany price are personally liable for the shortfall penalty if the company is used as a mere conduit and the transfer pricing adjustment exceeds the company’s ability to pay. The directors may be banned from undertaking management of the NZ company, their personal bank accounts may be subject to civil restraint orders, and if the arrangement involves false invoices or intentionally misleading the tax authority, they are subject to criminal prosecution under the Crimes Act 1961. Piercing the veil is available where the director has stripped the company of assets before payment of the adjusted tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False DTA Claim, Shell Company Treatment, and NRWT Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident corporate shareholder in a jurisdiction such as Hong Kong or the British Virgin Islands receives a NZD 5,000,000 dividend from the NZ Ltd and claims a 5% or 15% reduced treaty rate under the applicable DTA without providing a Tax Residency Certificate and without being the beneficial owner of the dividend. The shareholder is a shell with no employees, no economic activity, and no substance; the ultimate beneficial owner is located in a third country that has no treaty with New Zealand. The NZ company fails to withhold NRWT at the statutory rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will deny DTA relief under both the OECD MLI principal purpose test and domestic anti-avoidance rules. The company is liable for NRWT at the statutory 30% (or 15% if fully imputed) on the entire dividend, plus a 100% shortfall penalty for the abusive tax position and use-of-money interest. The Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes a separate absolute-liability penalty on any company that fails to withhold NRWT from a dividend or interest payment, equal to the amount of unpaid NRWT, and the Commissioner may recover the penalty from the directors personally as persons responsible for the company’s obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who arrange the dividend payment knowing the treaty claim is false are personally liable for the NRWT shortfall and penalties. The director may be blacklisted by Inland Revenue under the departure prohibition order regime and removed from the Companies Office directors register. Civil asset tracing may reach the director’s personal assets if the dividend was paid to a related offshore entity and then on-distributed to the director. Criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment for up to 7 years for evasion of payment of tax plus substantial restitution orders.
